Upon first glimpsing the valley, he later recounted, “The spirit of light rested upon me and hovered over the valley, and I felt that there the Saints would find protection and safety.”Manuscript History of Brigham Young 1846–1847,edited by Elden J. Watson (1971), 564.
Journal of Discourses,14:118.

The following spring (May 1848), hearing that enemies had expressed the fear that nothing could drive them from the Rocky Mountains if they were allowed to settle there, Brigham Young agreed: the Saints would never be driven from the mountains “unless they drive themselves. I prophe[s]y that myself.” It was his faith that “we shall go safe” and from there “preach to all nations the peaceable things of the K[ingdom].” Minutes, 14 May 1848, LDS Church Archives.
